meiji_transition.summary: Osaka-fu was set up in 1868; Sakai Prefecture (Izumi, Kawachi, Yamato) joined in 1881, and Yamato split off as Nara in 1887.
meiji_transition.boundary_note: Settsu Province is cut in two by the prefectural border — the east belongs to Osaka, the west (Kobe, Amagasaki, Nishinomiya…) to Hyōgo.

history_timeline.title: Naniwa Palace
history_timeline.summary: Naniwa-tsu was the ancient gateway port; Naniwa Nagara-Toyosaki Palace was built after 645, and Daisen Kofun (attributed to Emperor Nintoku) is Japan's largest keyhole tomb.

history_timeline.title: Kusunoki Masashige
history_timeline.summary: Kusunoki Masashige of Kawachi rose for Emperor Go-Daigo, holding off the shogunate's armies with clever tactics at Akasaka and Chihaya castles (1331–33).

history_timeline.title: The Hatakeyama and Sakai
history_timeline.summary: Masashige died at Minatogawa (1336) and his son Masatsura at Shijō-Nawate (1348); Kawachi was later ruled by the Hatakeyama, and Sakai rose as a port for trade with Ming China.

history_timeline.title: Ishiyama Hongan-ji
history_timeline.summary: Ishiyama Hongan-ji, head temple of the Ikkō sect, held out against Nobunaga for ten years (1570–1580); Hideyoshi built Osaka Castle on its site, and the Toyotomi fell in the Summer Siege of 1615.

history_timeline.title: Kitchen of the realm
history_timeline.summary: Osaka became Japan's logistics hub, lined with the domains' warehouses; the Dōjima Rice Exchange saw the world's first futures trading, and townspeople's culture flourished.

history_timeline.title: Greater Osaka
history_timeline.summary: In 1925 Osaka city briefly outnumbered Tokyo — 'Dai-Ōsaka'; it hosted world expos in 1970 and 2025.

dialect.name: Osaka dialect
dialect.features: Fast-paced and full of humor; 'ōkini' (thanks) and 'nande yanen' (why?!) are badges of its comic-retort culture.

guide.opening: Though I lived in Heian-kyō, I often sailed down to Naniwa-tsu. Later Lord Hideyoshi built the realm's greatest castle at Osaka — would you hear of its rise and fall?

regional_meme.title: No retort, no fun
regional_meme.text: In Osaka, a joke with no comeback is the ultimate rudeness — 'nande yanen' is everyday etiquette.

regional_meme.title: Which side of the escalator?
regional_meme.text: Osakans stand on the right of escalators, Tokyoites on the left — a classic Kantō–Kansai rivalry topic.

hero_persona.name: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
hero_persona.title: Unifier of the realm · the Taikō
hero_persona.opening_line: I am the Taikō, Toyotomi Hideyoshi! From a farm boy in Owari to ruler of the realm — and Osaka Castle is my masterpiece, glittering with gold!
hero_persona.tone_prompt: cheerful and outgoing, loves to show off, approachable yet shrewd; full of Osaka-merchant warmth

ramen.highlight: Workers' ramen from Takaida in East Osaka — dark broth, fat noodles

sake.taste_profile: Rich & dry: home-grown rice, all pure-rice, strongly aged character
